title: Amortized Variational Inference of Latent Intensities from Replicated Point Patterns
abstract: arXiv:2610.16669v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Bayesian inference for latent point process intensities often relies on per-dataset sampling or optimization, making repeated inference computationally expensive. We propose a neural-network-based amortized variational framework that learns a reusable inference rule mapping a variable number of replicated point patterns to a distribution over their shared latent intensity. Trained from event times using the point process likelihood, the model learns an amortized inference rule without ground-truth intensity supervision. At test time, it performs inference of the latent distribution in a forward pass. On synthetic data, additional realizations improve intensity recovery and yield narrower credible intervals with broadly stable coverage. Our method is tested on bicycle-sharing data and achieves the highest mean held-out log likelihood among the evaluated methods while requiring substantially less inference time than the Log-Gaussian Cox Pr

translated_title: 从重复点模式中对潜在强度进行摊销变分推断
translated_abstract: 对潜在点过程强度的贝叶斯推断通常依赖于针对每个数据集的采样或优化，使得重复推断在计算上非常昂贵。我们提出了一种基于神经网络的摊销变分框架，该框架学习一个可复用的推断规则，将可变数量的重复点模式映射到其共享潜在强度的分布上。该模型使用点过程似然从事件时间进行训练，在无需真实强度监督的情况下学习到摊销推断规则。在测试时，它只需一次前向传播即可完成潜在分布的推断。在合成数据上，更多的观测实现改善了强度恢复效果，并产生更窄的置信区间，同时覆盖率大体保持稳定。我们的方法在共享单车数据上进行了测试，在所评估的方法中取得了最高的平均留出对数似然，同时所需的推断时间远少于对数高斯Cox过程。
tldr: 提出了一种基于神经网络的摊销变分推断框架，无需真实强度监督即可从重复点模式中学习可复用的推断规则，通过一次前向传播完成潜在强度分布的贝叶斯推断，相比对数高斯Cox过程等方法速度大幅提升且推断精度更高。
en_tdlr: Proposes a neural-network-based amortized variational inference framework that learns a reusable inference rule from replicated point patterns without ground-truth supervision, enabling Bayesian inference of latent intensity distributions in a single forward pass, achieving higher accuracy and substantially faster inference than methods such as the Log-Gaussian Cox Process.
